# Dolby AC-4 with Dolby Atmos (ac4-atmos)

Dolby AC-4 with Dolby Atmos, written as `.ac4`. DeeZy uses DEE's level 3, for
film and TV. Every option is on
[deezy encode ac4-atmos](../cli/encode-ac4-atmos.md).

```bash
deezy encode ac4-atmos movie.mkv
deezy encode ac4-atmos --bitrate 768 master.wav
```

## Sources

The source is a TrueHD Atmos track (truehdd decodes it to a DAMF master first, so DeeZy needs truehdd), a DAMF master (the `.atmos` file, beside its `.atmos.metadata` and `.atmos.audio`) or an ADM BWF master (`.wav`).

## Data rates

<!-- BEGIN generated by scripts/cli_docs.py from 'deezy bitrates': edit deezy/dee/spec.py, not this block -->

```text {.scrollable-code-block}
ac4-atmos
  atmos default 448: 256, 320, 448, 768
```

<!-- END generated -->

DeeZy's default is a step above DEE's own, 320 kbps.

## Loudness and DRC

DEE only measures the loudness and writes it into the stream; `--loudness-preset`
works as for [Dolby Digital](dd.md#loudness). The four device DRC profiles are
`--flat-panel-drc`, `--home-theatre-drc`, `--portable-headphones-drc` and
`--portable-speakers-drc`.

## Warp mode

A TrueHD Atmos stream that carries no warp mode reaches DEE with none, which DEE renders as `warping`, its own default. `--thd-warp-mode` gives such a stream one (`normal`, `warping`, `prologiciix` or `loro`). A stream that has a warp mode keeps it. DeeZy 1.x gave every such stream `normal`.

## Sync

DeeZy compensates the delay DEE's manifest reports. It hasn't been checked
against an AC-4 decoder.
